description: REQ-003's Base-chain native-gas precondition (`baseGasBalance >= minGasWei`) and REQ-012(c)/verification-architecture.md's `checkSourceFunded(baseUsdcBalance, baseGasBalance, requiredBaseUnits, minGasWei)` signature use `minGasWei: bigint` as a fail-closed gating comparand across REQ-003 (EARS line 189-190, Acceptance Criteria line 206), REQ-004's generic edge-case row ('Gas shortfall on any intermediate chain'), and PROP-005 -- but `minGasWei`'s actual value, source, or computation method is never defined anywhere in either spec file. Grep across specs/behavioral-spec.md and specs/verification-architecture.md for 'minGasWei', 'GasEstimator', 'estimateGas', 'gasPrice', and 'MIN_GAS' finds zero definitional text: no literal constant declaration (contrast with SWAP_MAX_USD, which gets a full explicit treatment -- 'a literal constant in the pure module, never read from process.env or any genome/config file', 'defined once, in one file, with no second definition anywhere else', behavioral-spec.md:39-40, 307), no config/env source, and no effectful shell component (e.g. a gas-price oracle) listed in the Purity Boundary Map's Effectful Shell section (verification-architecture.md:31-49) that could supply it at runtime. REQ-003's own edge case explicitly states the stakes: 'Base USDC is sufficient but native ETH/gas for the Base-side approve+swap tx is insufficient: fail closed (a partially-fundable swap that dies mid-signature is worse than not starting)' (behavioral-spec.md:199-200) -- but this fail-closed guarantee is entirely dependent on `minGasWei` being set to a real, safe, non-trivial threshold. Because the spec never pins this value down (not even as 'TBD, sourced from config X' or 'a literal constant analogous to SWAP_MAX_USD'), a spec-compliant implementer has no way to know what value to hard-code, and nothing in the spec prevents an implementation from defaulting `minGasWei` to `0n` or an arbitrarily low value -- which would make the gas check vacuous, defeating REQ-003's own stated purpose ('a partially-fundable swap that dies mid-signature is worse than not starting'). For a money-path spec whose Context section states 'treat every REQ below as MUST, none is optional' (behavioral-spec.md:3), an undefined safety-gating constant is a genuine implementability gap, not a minor omission -- Dimension 1 of Phase 1c review explicitly asks 'are the requirements concrete enough to be implemented unambiguously?' and this one is not.

evidence.snippet: checkSourceFunded(baseUsdcBalance: bigint, baseGasBalance: bigint, requiredBaseUnits: bigint, minGasWei: bigint) ... AND the Base-chain native-gas balance (`baseGasBalance: bigint`) is `>= minGasWei: bigint` for leg 1 ... [no REQ, constant declaration, config source, or effectful component anywhere defines minGasWei's value]

fix: Give `minGasWei` the same explicit treatment REQ-006 gives `SWAP_MAX_USD`: either (a) declare it a literal constant defined once in the pure cap-enforcement module (or a sibling module), immune to env/config override, with an exact value stated in the spec and a PROP asserting that exact value, or (b) if it must be dynamically estimated (e.g. current Base gas price * expected gas units for an approve+swap), add an explicit effectful `GasEstimator`/equivalent component to the Purity Boundary Map's Effectful Shell section, name the formula, and add an acceptance criterion + PROP fixture pinning a concrete expected value the way PROP-022 pins `toBaseUnits(15.0, 6) === 15000000n`.
